title: How to Start Any Conversation the Right Way | Chris Fenning | TED
speaker: TED
zh: 【TED】如何以正確的方式開始任何對話 |克里斯芬寧 |泰德（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: I want to be long-winded and unclear.
cues.en: I want to be long-winded and unclear.
cues.zh: 我想囉嗦又不清楚。

cues.text: It's not a common opening line.
cues.en: It's not a common opening line.
cues.zh: 這不是常見的開場白。

cues.text: Most people won't tell us when they're going to be long-winded,
cues.en: Most people won't tell us when they're going to be long-winded,
cues.zh: 大多數人不會告訴我們他們什麼時候會囉嗦，

cues.text: but we know.
cues.en: but we know.
cues.zh: 但我們知道。

cues.text: We can tell pretty quickly if someone’s going to get to the point
cues.en: We can tell pretty quickly if someone’s going to get to the point
cues.zh: 我們可以很快判斷某人是否能切入主題

cues.text: or if we are in for a long and painful conversation.
cues.en: or if we are in for a long and painful conversation.
cues.zh: 或者如果我們正在進行一場漫長而痛苦的談話。

cues.text: And this is especially true at work.
cues.en: And this is especially true at work.
cues.zh: 在工作中尤其如此。

cues.text: Every year, poor communication costs businesses hundreds of billions of dollars
cues.en: Every year, poor communication costs businesses hundreds of billions of dollars
cues.zh: 每年，溝通不良都會對企業造成數千億美元的損失

cues.text: in lost productivity.
cues.en: in lost productivity.
cues.zh: 生產力損失。

cues.text: And I have to confess, the early part of my career,
cues.en: And I have to confess, the early part of my career,
cues.zh: 我必須承認，在我職業生涯的早期，

cues.text: I was responsible for at least some of that.
cues.en: I was responsible for at least some of that.
cues.zh: 我至少對其中的一部分負有責任。

cues.text: But I'm not alone.
cues.en: But I'm not alone.
cues.zh: 但我並不孤單。

cues.text: Hands up if you work with someone who is long winded or unclear.
cues.en: Hands up if you work with someone who is long winded or unclear.
cues.zh: 如果您與囉嗦或不清楚的人一起工作，請舉手。

cues.text: That's a lot of hands.
cues.en: That's a lot of hands.
cues.zh: 這是很多手。

cues.text: Now I’m sure we are all thinking about people outside this room, right?
cues.en: Now I’m sure we are all thinking about people outside this room, right?
cues.zh: 現在我確信我們都在想這個房間外面的人，對吧？

cues.text: Except for those of you pointing at each other.
cues.en: Except for those of you pointing at each other.
cues.zh: 除了你們互相指指點點的人。

cues.text: But what would happen if we asked the people outside this room?
cues.en: But what would happen if we asked the people outside this room?
cues.zh: 但如果我們問這個房間外面的人會發生什麼事呢？

cues.text: They might be thinking about us.
cues.en: They might be thinking about us.
cues.zh: 他們可能正在考慮我們。

cues.text: And while our goal is to be clear and concise, do we really know how?
cues.en: And while our goal is to be clear and concise, do we really know how?
cues.zh: 雖然我們的目標是清晰簡潔，但我們真的知道如何做嗎？

cues.text: Every time we communicate, we have an opportunity to create clarity
cues.en: Every time we communicate, we have an opportunity to create clarity
cues.zh: 每次我們溝通時，我們都有機會澄清問題

cues.text: or confusion.
cues.en: or confusion.
cues.zh: 或混亂。

cues.text: And clarity begins from the very first minute.
cues.en: And clarity begins from the very first minute.
cues.zh: 清晰從第一分鐘就開始了。

cues.text: If you get the first minute right, you set your conversation up for success.
cues.en: If you get the first minute right, you set your conversation up for success.
cues.zh: 如果你在第一分鐘就做好了準備，你的談話就會成功。

cues.text: Get it wrong your conversations will be longer, less effective
cues.en: Get it wrong your conversations will be longer, less effective
cues.zh: 搞錯了，你的談話會變得更長、效率更低

cues.text: and more frustrating.
cues.en: and more frustrating.
cues.zh: 更令人沮喪。

cues.text: Now on the off chance we could all use a little more clarity,
cues.en: Now on the off chance we could all use a little more clarity,
cues.zh: 現在，如果我們都可以更清晰一點的話，

cues.text: I'm going to share a tip with you today.
cues.en: I'm going to share a tip with you today.
cues.zh: 今天要跟大家分享一個秘訣。

cues.text: A tip that will help each of you improve the success
cues.en: A tip that will help each of you improve the success
cues.zh: 一個將幫助你們每個人提高成功率的技巧

cues.text: of your communication at work.
cues.en: of your communication at work.
cues.zh: 您在工作上的溝通。

cues.text: A tip that has been tested by more than 75,000 people around the world.
cues.en: A tip that has been tested by more than 75,000 people around the world.
cues.zh: 該技巧已經過全球超過 75,000 人的測試。

cues.text: And a tip that will help each of you get the first minute right.
cues.en: And a tip that will help each of you get the first minute right.
cues.zh: 還有一個技巧可以幫助你們每個人在第一分鐘就做好準備。

cues.text: And here it is.
cues.en: And here it is.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.text: There are three things we must include at the start of our work messages.
cues.en: There are three things we must include at the start of our work messages.
cues.zh: 我們必須在工作資訊的開頭包含三件事。

cues.text: And those three things begin with T, I and P.
cues.en: And those three things begin with T, I and P.
cues.zh: 這三件事以 T、I 和 P 開頭。

cues.text: It's a TIP.
cues.en: It's a TIP.
cues.zh: 這是一個提示。

cues.text: Now the first part of the tip is the T, and T stands for topic.
cues.en: Now the first part of the tip is the T, and T stands for topic.
cues.zh: 現在提示的第一部分是T，T代表主題。

cues.text: Every conversation at work needs a clear topic.
cues.en: Every conversation at work needs a clear topic.
cues.zh: 工作中的每次談話都需要一個明確的話題。

cues.text: When the topic is clear, everyone knows what we're talking about.
cues.en: When the topic is clear, everyone knows what we're talking about.
cues.zh: 當主題明確時，每個人都知道我們在說什麼。

cues.text: Everyone's in sync.
cues.en: Everyone's in sync.
cues.zh: 每個人都同步。

cues.text: Everybody understands.
cues.en: Everybody understands.
cues.zh: 大家都明白。

cues.text: Unfortunately, reality isn't always like this, is it?
cues.en: Unfortunately, reality isn't always like this, is it?
cues.zh: 不幸的是，現實並不總是這樣，不是嗎？

cues.text: How often are you in a conversation and you find yourself thinking,
cues.en: How often are you in a conversation and you find yourself thinking,
cues.zh: 你有多少次在談話中發現自己在想，

cues.text: what are you talking about?
cues.en: what are you talking about?
cues.zh: 你在說什麼？

cues.text: That happens when the topic is not clear.
cues.en: That happens when the topic is not clear.
cues.zh: 當主題不明確時就會發生這種情況。

cues.text: Now usually the consequences are pretty minor -- a little bit of wasted time, some minor frustration --
cues.en: Now usually the consequences are pretty minor -- a little bit of wasted time, some minor frustration --
cues.zh: 現在通常後果都很輕微——浪費一點時間，一些輕微的挫折感——

cues.text: but sometimes, the consequences are more significant.
cues.en: but sometimes, the consequences are more significant.
cues.zh: 但有時，後果更為嚴重。

cues.text: In 2006, I was part of an engineering team writing a bid --
cues.en: In 2006, I was part of an engineering team writing a bid --
cues.zh: 2006 年，我是一個工程團隊的一員，負責撰寫標書——

cues.text: a proposal -- that was worth a lot of money to our company.
cues.en: a proposal -- that was worth a lot of money to our company.
cues.zh: 一個提案——這對我們公司來說值很多錢。

cues.text: And a couple of days before the big meeting, my boss came up to me and said,
cues.en: And a couple of days before the big meeting, my boss came up to me and said,
cues.zh: 在大型會議前幾天，我的老闆走過來對我說：

cues.text: "Hey, Chris, I need you to change the meeting from Tuesday to Thursday." So off I went and I changed the meeting.
cues.en: "Hey, Chris, I need you to change the meeting from Tuesday to Thursday." So off I went and I changed the meeting.
cues.zh: 「嘿，克里斯，我需要你把會議從週二改到週四。」所以我離開了，並改變了會議。

cues.text: I typed an email, sent it to the client saying, "Something’s come up, we've got to change."
cues.en: I typed an email, sent it to the client saying, "Something’s come up, we've got to change."
cues.zh: 我寫了一封電子郵件，傳送給客戶，說：“出現了一些問題，我們必須做出改變。”

cues.text: And about a minute after I hit send, my phone rings.
cues.en: And about a minute after I hit send, my phone rings.
cues.zh: 在我點選傳送後大約一分鐘，我的手機響了。

cues.text: It's my boss.
cues.en: It's my boss.
cues.zh: 這是我的老闆。

cues.text: He had one question: "Why did you change the meeting?"
cues.en: He had one question: "Why did you change the meeting?"
cues.zh: 他有一個問題：“你為什麼改變會議？”

cues.text: You see, he was talking about our one-to-one,
cues.en: You see, he was talking about our one-to-one,
cues.zh: 你看，他在談論我們的一對一，

cues.text: and I was thinking about the client meeting.
cues.en: and I was thinking about the client meeting.
cues.zh: 我正在考慮客戶會議。

cues.text: The lack of a clear topic meant he and I were thinking about two very different things.
cues.en: The lack of a clear topic meant he and I were thinking about two very different things.
cues.zh: 缺乏明確的主題意味著他和我正在思考兩件截然不同的事情。

cues.text: Now that might be the single biggest contribution I’ve made to the cost of bad communication,
cues.en: Now that might be the single biggest contribution I’ve made to the cost of bad communication,
cues.zh: 現在，這可能是我對不良溝通成本做出的最大貢獻，

cues.text: but it also marks the moment at which I began to be interested in improving how we communicate at work.
cues.en: but it also marks the moment at which I began to be interested in improving how we communicate at work.
cues.zh: 但這也標誌著我開始對改善工作溝通方式感興趣的那一刻。

cues.text: So all our messages have to begin with a clear topic.
cues.en: So all our messages have to begin with a clear topic.
cues.zh: 因此，我們所有的訊息都必須以一個明確的主題開始。

cues.text: But how? How do we do this?
cues.en: But how? How do we do this?
cues.zh: 但如何呢？我們該怎麼做呢？

cues.text: It's really easy.
cues.en: It's really easy.
cues.zh: 這真的很容易。

cues.text: Start your message with one sentence that names the topic you want to talk about,
cues.en: Start your message with one sentence that names the topic you want to talk about,
cues.zh: 用一句話開始你的訊息，說出你想談論的主題，

cues.text: and the more specific, the better.
cues.en: and the more specific, the better.
cues.zh: 而且越具體越好。

cues.text: You could say, "I'd like to talk about July sales figures." "I want to talk about Project Everest's timeline."
cues.en: You could say, "I'd like to talk about July sales figures." "I want to talk about Project Everest's timeline."
cues.zh: 您可以說：“我想談談 7 月份的銷售資料。” “我想談談珠穆朗瑪峰計劃的時間表。”

cues.text: Or "Can I talk about our one-to-one this week?" One message, one sentence
cues.en: Or "Can I talk about our one-to-one this week?" One message, one sentence
cues.zh: 或「我可以談談我們這週的一對一嗎？」一則訊息，一句話

cues.text: that lets your audience know what the topic is.
cues.en: that lets your audience know what the topic is.
cues.zh: 讓你的聽眾知道主題是什麼。

cues.text: They won't be thinking, "What are you talking about?"
cues.en: They won't be thinking, "What are you talking about?"
cues.zh: 他們不會想：“你在說什麼？”

cues.text: Now having a clear topic is a great start, but it's not enough.
cues.en: Now having a clear topic is a great start, but it's not enough.
cues.zh: 現在有一個明確的主題是一個很好的開始，但這還不夠。

cues.text: We need the second part of the tip, which is the I.
cues.en: We need the second part of the tip, which is the I.
cues.zh: 我們需要提示的第二部分，即 I。

cues.text: And I stands for intent.
cues.en: And I stands for intent.
cues.zh: 我代表意圖。

cues.text: Intent is what we want the other person to do with our message.
cues.en: Intent is what we want the other person to do with our message.
cues.zh: 意圖是我們希望對方對我們的訊息做什麼。

cues.text: Have you ever been in a conversation and a few minutes in thought, "Why are you telling me this?"
cues.en: Have you ever been in a conversation and a few minutes in thought, "Why are you telling me this?"
cues.zh: 你是否曾經在一次談話中思考過幾分鐘，“你為什麼要告訴我這個？”

cues.text: That happens when the intent isn't clear, when the speaker hasn't told you what to do
cues.en: That happens when the intent isn't clear, when the speaker hasn't told you what to do
cues.zh: 當意圖不明確、說話者沒有告訴你該怎麼做時，就會發生這種情況

cues.text: with the information that they are giving you.
cues.en: with the information that they are giving you.
cues.zh: 以及他們向您提供的資訊。

cues.text: Now there’s a process in our brains called selective attention,
cues.en: Now there’s a process in our brains called selective attention,
cues.zh: 現在我們的大腦中有一個過程叫做選擇性注意，

cues.text: and this filters incoming information and tells you what is important
cues.en: and this filters incoming information and tells you what is important
cues.zh: 這會過濾傳入的訊息並告訴您什麼是重要的

cues.text: and what is not.
cues.en: and what is not.
cues.zh: 以及什麼不是。

cues.text: And if you don't know what to do with a message, your brain says, not important.
cues.en: And if you don't know what to do with a message, your brain says, not important.
cues.zh: 如果你不知道如何處理一則訊息，你的大腦會說，這並不重要。

cues.text: And we stop listening.
cues.en: And we stop listening.
cues.zh: 我們就不再聽了。

cues.text: At the beginning of this talk, I told you I would give you a tip that would help improve the success of your communication at work.
cues.en: At the beginning of this talk, I told you I would give you a tip that would help improve the success of your communication at work.
cues.zh: 在演講開始時，我告訴你我會給你一個技巧，幫助你提高工作中溝通的成功率。

cues.text: That told your brains what to do with this information.
cues.en: That told your brains what to do with this information.
cues.zh: 這告訴你的大腦如何處理這些資訊。

cues.text: If I hadn't done that, I could be faced with a room full of people smiling politely
cues.en: If I hadn't done that, I could be faced with a room full of people smiling politely
cues.zh: 如果我不這樣做，我可能會面對滿屋子的人禮貌地微笑

cues.text: while all thinking, "Why are you telling us this?" Now that is something we want to avoid at work.
cues.en: while all thinking, "Why are you telling us this?" Now that is something we want to avoid at work.
cues.zh: 大家都在想：「為什麼要告訴我們這些？」這是我們在工作中要避免的事情。

cues.text: But there is another, and perhaps more important reason to make your intent clear.
cues.en: But there is another, and perhaps more important reason to make your intent clear.
cues.zh: 但還有另一個也許更重要的原因可以明確你的意圖。

cues.text: You want to avoid frustrating the people you're talking to.
cues.en: You want to avoid frustrating the people you're talking to.
cues.zh: 您希望避免讓與您交談的人感到沮喪。

cues.text: I'd had a particularly bad day, and I walked into my colleague Tina's office,
cues.en: I'd had a particularly bad day, and I walked into my colleague Tina's office,
cues.zh: 我度過了特別糟糕的一天，我走進同事蒂娜的辦公室，

cues.text: and I sat down with my head in my hands, and I told her how I'd messed up on an important call with a senior leader.
cues.en: and I sat down with my head in my hands, and I told her how I'd messed up on an important call with a senior leader.
cues.zh: 我坐下來，雙手抱頭，告訴她我是如何在與一位高階主管的重要通話中搞砸的。

cues.text: And when I finished talking, Tina very, very helpfully said, "Oh, why don't you try this and maybe we can avoid this next time."
cues.en: And when I finished talking, Tina very, very helpfully said, "Oh, why don't you try this and maybe we can avoid this next time."
cues.zh: 當我說完後，蒂娜非常非常樂於助人地說：“哦，你為什麼不試試這個，也許我們下次可以避免這種情況。”

cues.text: And she was giving me all sorts of advice.
cues.en: And she was giving me all sorts of advice.
cues.zh: 她給了我各種各樣的建議。

cues.text: The more she spoke, the more frustrated I became.
cues.en: The more she spoke, the more frustrated I became.
cues.zh: 她越說，我就越沮喪。

cues.text: I didn't want her help.
cues.en: I didn't want her help.
cues.zh: 我不需要她的幫助。

cues.text: And that must have been quite obvious because she just put up her hands and said,
cues.en: And that must have been quite obvious because she just put up her hands and said,
cues.zh: 這一定是非常明顯的，因為她只是舉起手說，

cues.text: "You clearly don't want my help.
cues.en: "You clearly don't want my help.
cues.zh: 「你顯然不需要我的幫助。

cues.text: So why are you here?" I said, "Tina, I'm really sorry.
cues.en: So why are you here?" I said, "Tina, I'm really sorry.
cues.zh: 那你為什麼在這裡？ 」我說：「蒂娜，我真的很抱歉。

cues.text: I just want to get this off my chest.
cues.en: I just want to get this off my chest.
cues.zh: 我只是想把這件事從心裡吐出來。

cues.text: Can I just talk for a minute?" And like a mother talking to a small child,
cues.en: Can I just talk for a minute?" And like a mother talking to a small child,
cues.zh: 我可以講一分鐘嗎？ 」就像母親對小孩子說話一樣，

cues.text: she rolled her eyes and said, "Well, why didn't you start with that?"
cues.en: she rolled her eyes and said, "Well, why didn't you start with that?"
cues.zh: 她翻了個白眼，說：“那你為什麼不從這個開始呢？”

cues.text: We need to tell our audience what to do with the information we're giving them.
cues.en: We need to tell our audience what to do with the information we're giving them.
cues.zh: 我們需要告訴觀眾如何處理我們提供給他們的資訊。

cues.text: Tina was working hard from the moment I started talking.
cues.en: Tina was working hard from the moment I started talking.
cues.zh: 從我開始說話的那一刻起，蒂娜就在努力工作。

cues.text: And all the way through, she was working hard to help me and I didn't want or need that.
cues.en: And all the way through, she was working hard to help me and I didn't want or need that.
cues.zh: 自始至終，她都在努力幫助我，而我不想也不需要這樣。

cues.text: She was annoyed and rightly so.
cues.en: She was annoyed and rightly so.
cues.zh: 她很生氣，也是理所當然的。

cues.text: So when you start your message, after you've given a clear topic, tell your audience what to do with it.
cues.en: So when you start your message, after you've given a clear topic, tell your audience what to do with it.
cues.zh: 因此，當您開始發布訊息時，在給出明確的主題後，請告訴您的聽眾如何處理它。

cues.text: And again, you can do this with one line.
cues.en: And again, you can do this with one line.
cues.zh: 再說一遍，您只需一行即可完成此操作。

cues.text: Make your intent clear.
cues.en: Make your intent clear.
cues.zh: 明確你的意圖。

cues.text: If you have a question, say, "Can I ask you a question?"
cues.en: If you have a question, say, "Can I ask you a question?"
cues.zh: 如果你有問題，請說：“我可以問你一個問題嗎？”

cues.text: If you want someone to make a decision, say, "I'd like your help with this decision."
cues.en: If you want someone to make a decision, say, "I'd like your help with this decision."
cues.zh: 如果你想讓別人做出決定，可以說：“我需要你幫助做出這個決定。”

cues.text: If you want to get something off your chest, just say, "Is it OK if I vent for a minute?"
cues.en: If you want to get something off your chest, just say, "Is it OK if I vent for a minute?"
cues.zh: 如果你想吐露心聲，只需說：“我可以發洩一下嗎？”

cues.text: If you tell your audience what to do with your message, not only will their brains pay more attention,
cues.en: If you tell your audience what to do with your message, not only will their brains pay more attention,
cues.zh: 如果你告訴你的聽眾如何處理你的訊息，他們的大腦不僅會更加註意，

cues.text: you will avoid frustrating them.
cues.en: you will avoid frustrating them.
cues.zh: 你會避免讓他們感到沮喪。

cues.text: That's kind of useful.
cues.en: That's kind of useful.
cues.zh: 這很有用。

cues.text: So we've made our topic clear.
cues.en: So we've made our topic clear.
cues.zh: 所以我們已經明確了我們的主題。

cues.text: We've told our audience what we intend for them to do.
cues.en: We've told our audience what we intend for them to do.
cues.zh: 我們已經告訴觀眾我們打算讓他們做什麼。

cues.text: It's time to get down into the detail, right?
cues.en: It's time to get down into the detail, right?
cues.zh: 是時候深入瞭解細節了，對吧？

cues.text: Get into the message.
cues.en: Get into the message.
cues.zh: 進入留言區。

cues.text: Wrong.
cues.en: Wrong.
cues.zh: 錯誤的。

cues.text: This is where we need the third part of the tip.
cues.en: This is where we need the third part of the tip.
cues.zh: 這是我們需要提示的第三部分的地方。

cues.text: The P.
cues.en: The P.
cues.zh: P。

cues.text: And P stands for point.
cues.en: And P stands for point.
cues.zh: P代表點。

cues.text: Point is the most important part of our message.
cues.en: Point is the most important part of our message.
cues.zh: 要點是我們資訊中最重要的部分。

cues.text: If you only had five seconds to speak, it's what you would say.
cues.en: If you only had five seconds to speak, it's what you would say.
cues.zh: 如果你只有五秒鐘的時間說話，那就是你想說的。

cues.text: And usually it's what your audience cares about the most.
cues.en: And usually it's what your audience cares about the most.
cues.zh: 通常這是觀眾最關心的。

cues.text: When I was a kid, my dad played a game with me.
cues.en: When I was a kid, my dad played a game with me.
cues.zh: 當我還是個孩子的時候，我爸爸和我玩一個遊戲。

cues.text: If we were going on a journey, I'd go, "Dad, where are we going?" And he'd say, "Well, first, we're going to the car
cues.en: If we were going on a journey, I'd go, "Dad, where are we going?" And he'd say, "Well, first, we're going to the car
cues.zh: 如果我們要去旅行，我會問：「爸爸，我們要去哪裡？」他會說，「好吧，首先，我們要去汽車

cues.text: and then we’ll get in the car, leave the driveway, turn left onto the main street until we get to the post office,
cues.en: and then we’ll get in the car, leave the driveway, turn left onto the main street until we get to the post office,
cues.zh: 然後我們上車，離開車道，左轉進入主要街道，直到我們到達郵局，

cues.text: and then turn right until we go to a big yellow building." I just wanted to scream, "Where are we going?"
cues.en: and then turn right until we go to a big yellow building." I just wanted to scream, "Where are we going?"
cues.zh: 然後右轉，直到我們到達一座黃色的大建築。 」我只想尖叫，「我們要去哪裡？ 」

cues.text: I wanted the short version.
cues.en: I wanted the short version.
cues.zh: 我想要簡短的版本。

cues.text: I think he just wanted to wind me up a little bit.
cues.en: I think he just wanted to wind me up a little bit.
cues.zh: 我想他只是想讓我有點生氣。

cues.text: But fast forward a few years, I was doing the same thing at work.
cues.en: But fast forward a few years, I was doing the same thing at work.
cues.zh: 但幾年後，我在工作上也做了同樣的事情。

cues.text: Someone would ask me a question, or I’d start a conversation, and I would give all the detail,
cues.en: Someone would ask me a question, or I’d start a conversation, and I would give all the detail,
cues.zh: 有人會問我一個問題，或者我會開始對話，我會提供所有細節，

cues.text: step by step information.
cues.en: step by step information.
cues.zh: 一步一步的資訊。

cues.text: And every so often -- OK, quite often -- people would say, "Chris, just get to the point."
cues.en: And every so often -- OK, quite often -- people would say, "Chris, just get to the point."
cues.zh: 每隔一段時間——好吧，很多時候——人們會說，「克里斯，直奔主題吧。 」

cues.text: And that's what we need.
cues.en: And that's what we need.
cues.zh: 這就是我們所需要的。

cues.text: We need a point, we need a headline, something that tells us where this conversation is going.
cues.en: We need a point, we need a headline, something that tells us where this conversation is going.
cues.zh: 我們需要一個觀點，我們需要一個標題，需要一些東西來告訴我們這次談話的進展。

cues.text: Now, of course, there's a lot more information we could include, but that comes later.
cues.en: Now, of course, there's a lot more information we could include, but that comes later.
cues.zh: 當然，現在我們可以包含更多資訊，但這些資訊稍後再說。

cues.text: That comes after we've set up the audience to understand what the conversation is about.
cues.en: That comes after we've set up the audience to understand what the conversation is about.
cues.zh: 這是在我們讓觀眾瞭解對話的內容之後進行的。

cues.text: And we can do this quite simply, as the military likes to say,
cues.en: And we can do this quite simply, as the military likes to say,
cues.zh: 我們可以很簡單地做到這一點，正如軍方喜歡說的那樣，

cues.text: “Put the bottom line up front.” In one sentence,
cues.en: “Put the bottom line up front.” In one sentence,
cues.zh: 「把底線放在前面。 」用一句話來說，

cues.text: deliver the most important piece of information.
cues.en: deliver the most important piece of information.
cues.zh: 傳遞最重要的訊息。

cues.text: "I want to give a refund for a late delivery." "Our project launch is going to be delayed by a month."
cues.en: "I want to give a refund for a late delivery." "Our project launch is going to be delayed by a month."
cues.zh: 「我想為延遲交貨退款。 ” “我們的專案啟動將推遲一個月。 」

cues.text: Say the most important thing, and your audience will know where that conversation is going
cues.en: Say the most important thing, and your audience will know where that conversation is going
cues.zh: 說最重要的事情，你的聽眾就會知道談話的進展

cues.text: and they won't be thinking, "What is your point?" Now if you start your conversation with topic, intent and point,
cues.en: and they won't be thinking, "What is your point?" Now if you start your conversation with topic, intent and point,
cues.zh: 他們不會想：「你的觀點是什麼？ 「現在，如果你以主題、意圖和要點開始談話，

cues.text: you are starting with a clear and concise introduction, an introduction that answers the three questions we all have:
cues.en: you are starting with a clear and concise introduction, an introduction that answers the three questions we all have:
cues.zh: 您將從清晰簡潔的介紹開始，該介紹回答了我們所有人都提出的三個問題：

cues.text: What are you talking about?
cues.en: What are you talking about?
cues.zh: 你在說什麼？

cues.text: Why are you telling me this?
cues.en: Why are you telling me this?
cues.zh: 為什麼告訴我這個？

cues.text: And what is your point?
cues.en: And what is your point?
cues.zh: 你的觀點是什麼？

cues.text: Because here's the truth.
cues.en: Because here's the truth.
cues.zh: 因為這是事實。

cues.text: Every time we communicate, it is an opportunity to create clarity
cues.en: Every time we communicate, it is an opportunity to create clarity
cues.zh: 每次我們溝通，都是澄清問題的機會

cues.text: or confusion.
cues.en: or confusion.
cues.zh: 或混亂。

cues.text: And topic, intent and point is clarity.
cues.en: And topic, intent and point is clarity.
cues.zh: 主題、意圖和要點都很明確。

cues.text: So I have a challenge for you.
cues.en: So I have a challenge for you.
cues.zh: 所以我要給你一個挑戰。

cues.text: The next time you start a conversation at work, the next time you write a message,
cues.en: The next time you start a conversation at work, the next time you write a message,
cues.zh: 下次當你在工作中開始對話時，下次你寫訊息時，

cues.text: take a moment and think to yourself, what is my topic?
cues.en: take a moment and think to yourself, what is my topic?
cues.zh: 花點時間思考一下，我的主題是什麼？

cues.text: What do I intend for the other person to do with this message?
cues.en: What do I intend for the other person to do with this message?
cues.zh: 我想讓對方如何處理此訊息？

cues.text: And what point do I want to deliver?
cues.en: And what point do I want to deliver?
cues.zh: 我想傳達什麼觀點？

cues.text: Imagine working somewhere where everybody did this.
cues.en: Imagine working somewhere where everybody did this.
cues.zh: 想像一下在每個人都這樣做的地方工作。

cues.text: Imagine if everyone always knew what to do with the message you gave them,
cues.en: Imagine if everyone always knew what to do with the message you gave them,
cues.zh: 想像一下，如果每個人都知道如何處理你給他們的訊息，

cues.text: or understood what it was about.
cues.en: or understood what it was about.
cues.zh: 或明白它的意思。

cues.text: How much smoother, how much easier would our jobs be?
cues.en: How much smoother, how much easier would our jobs be?
cues.zh: 我們的工作會變得更順利、輕鬆多少？

cues.text: That, ladies and gentlemen, is the power of the first minute.
cues.en: That, ladies and gentlemen, is the power of the first minute.
cues.zh: 女士們先生們，這就是第一分鐘的力量。

cues.text: Thank you.
cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 謝謝。
